 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S. 173(1) OF M.V.ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 17.03.2014 PASSED IN M.V.C.NO.587/2009 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MACT, MANDYA, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.3,07,000/- WITH INTEREST @ 6% P.A FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL PAYMENT.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This matter is listed for admission today.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.

2. This Court, vide order dated 13.01.2023 made it clear that, if the learned counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.1 and 2 does not appear on the next date of hearing, the matter will be heard in his absence.
Inspite of the said order, learned counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.1 and 2 is absent and not pursuing the matter diligently.

3. This appeal is filed challenging the judgment and award dated 17.03.2014 passed in M.V.C.No.587/2009 on the file of the Principal Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and MACT, Mandya ('the Tribunal' for short)
4.

The factual matrix of the case of the claimants before the Tribunal is that on 15.07.2009, the deceased K.R. Raju was riding the motorcycle from Mysuru towards Mandya near Gowdahally Gate of Mysuru-Bengaluru Road and at that time, a cyclist came across the road all of a sudden and the deceased, in order to avoid dashing against the cyclist, took the vehicle towards his left side and lost control and fell down along with motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries to head and died at the spot.

sentences.text: 2 5 . It is the claim of the claimants before the Tribunal that the deceased Raju was aged about 22 years and was doing petty business, earning Rs.3,000/- per month and the claimants were entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased for their livelihood and hence, they have lost the earning member of the family.

6. In pursuance of the claim petition, the first respondent in the written statement contended that the vehicle was insured with the insurance company and the same is valid and the rider of the motorcycle took the same for work as per his direction and death has arisen out of use of motorcycle.

7. The respondent No.2-insurance company in the written statement admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the motorcycle and contended that the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.2- insurance company also disputed the relationship between the claimants and the deceased and contended that the deceased was not holding any valid and effective driving license.

It is also contended that the deceased is not the owner of the vehicle and he had borrowed the vehicle from the owner and he is not an employee of the owner of the motorcycle.
8.
The claimants, in order to substantiate their contention, examined the first claimant as P.W.1 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P7.

On the other hand, the respondents have not led any evidence but, got marked the copy of the policy as Ex.R1.
9.

The Tribunal, after considering both oral and documentary evidence placed on record, awarded compensation of Rs.3,07,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and fastened the liability on the insurance company.
Hence, the present appeal is filed.

10. The main contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company in the appeal is that the petition is filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicle Act and the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

The Tribunal failed to take note of the said fact into consideration and the award passed by the Tribunal against the appellant herein is contrary to law and ought to have dismissed the appeal against the insurance company.
The counsel would vehemently contend that when the borrower stepped into the shoes of the owner, he cannot claim any compensation against the insurance company.

The counsel also vehemently contend that with regard to the PA coverage of the owner of the vehicle is concerned, a premium of Rs.50/- is collected from the insurer and at the most the liability is to the extent of Rs.1,00,000/- in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of RAMKHILADI.
Hence, it requires interference.

11. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and also on perusal of the material available on record it discloses that in the claim petition it is specifically mentioned that the deceased was running a petty shop and earning Rs.3,000/- per month.
No doubt, respondent No.1 has filed written statement stating that the deceased went in the motorcycle as per his direction to his work.
But in order to prove that he was employed with respondent No.1, no material is placed before the Court except filing of the written statement and he also not adduced any evidence.

It is also important to note that in the pleadings itself, the claimants have stated that the deceased was United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri K Ramakrishna on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73661973/
3 running a petty shop and earning Rs.3,000/- per month.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri K Ramakrishna on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When such being the case, the objection statement of respondent No.1 cannot be accepted.
No doubt, the question of negligence does not arise when the petition is filed under Section 163 (A) of MV Act and the Court also taken note of the document at Ex.R1.
On perusal of Ex.R1-policy copy it discloses that an amount of Rs.50/- was collected compulsory PA to owner not the driver to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-.

The material also discloses that in the written statement specifically defence was taken by the insurance company that the deceased had borrowed the vehicle from respondent No.1 when an accident was taken place.

When such being the material available on record, when the claimants themselves pleaded that the deceased was not an employee but he was running a petty shop and earning Rs.3,000/- and the fact that the vehicle belongs to respondent No.1 is not in dispute, hence, it is clear that the deceased was the borrower of the vehicle.

12. In view of the judgment of NINGAMMA AND ANOTHER vs UNITED INDIA INSURANCE CO.
LTD.
reported in 2009 ACJ 2020 and also the judgment of RAMKHILADI AND ANOTHER v. UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY AND ANTOHER reported in (2020) 2 SCC 550, there is an explicit contract between the owner and the insurer and when they have collected the premium of Rs.50/- to cover the risk of the owner and when the borrower stepped into the shoes of the owner, the judgment and award of the Tribunal requires to be modified and the liability has to be fastened only against the insurance company to the extent of payment of compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- with interest in view of collecting of Rs.50/- as premium.

13. In view of the discussions made above, I pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the  Tribunal dated 17.03.2014 passed in MVC  No.57/2009 is modified granting compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- as against Rs.3,07,000/- with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
(iii) The Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation amount with interest within six weeks from today.

(iv) The amount in deposit made by the Insurance Company is ordered to be United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri K Ramakrishna on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73661973/
4 transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.

(vi) With regard to the release and keeping the amount in Fixed Deposit, the order of the Tribunal is modified to release the entire amount in favour of the claimants equally, since the amount is reduced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
